Stray Kids Albums, TWICE Concerts, & More — JYP Entertainment’s Planned Activities For Each Artist In 2025
==========================================================================================================

Fans can’t wait to see it all 🔥

![Image 3](https://image.koreaboo.com/2025/03/jyp25plans-FI.jpg)

[News](https://www.koreaboo.com/news/)

![Image 4](https://www.koreaboo.com/wp-content/themes/KbooOS2/img/site_icon/koreaboo36.png)

Koreaboo

March 17th, 2025

**JYP****Entertainment** has outlined its plans for 2025, revealing what fans can expect from each of its artists. From world tours to new album releases, the company’s fourth-quarter results report for 2024 gave fans insight into the busy schedules ahead.

![Image 5: jypplans24-FI](https://image.koreaboo.com/2025/03/jypplans24-FI-925x486.jpg)

| _JYP Entertainment_

DAY6
----

The band made history as the first to hold a concert at the Gocheok Sky Dome in 2024. In 2025, they will continue their massive world tour and are set to perform at a stadium in Jakarta this May.

TWICE
-----

TWICE members will take part in a mix of group, unit, and solo projects. Their sub-unit, **Misamo**, achieved an impressive milestone by performing six dome concerts in three Japanese cities. A new world tour is also expected in 2025.

Stray Kids
----------

Stray Kids are experiencing record-breaking success, with their recent tour drawing over 2.2 million attendees across 55 shows in 34 locations. They continue to dominate U.S. sales charts, ranking second in overall CD sales and first among K-Pop artists. Additionally, they have topped the Billboard 200 with six consecutive albums and appeared on the Billboard Hot 100 three times in a row. In 2025, they will release two new albums and aim to reach even more miletones.

ITZY
----

Fans can look forward to both group and solo activities, with new albums and tours scheduled for 2025. With Yeji already in the middle of promoting her solo debut, will fans see another solo debut in the horizon?

NMIXX
-----

The group plans to release a mini-album and hold fan concerts in Latin America and Asia. Their growing popularity has also led to increased advertisement deals.

KickFlip
--------

Named one of the “Top 8 K-Pop Rookies to Watch in 2025” by the Recording Academy, KickFlip has been gaining traction both domestically and globally, especially in streaming. They recently hit one million TikTok followers.

NiziU
-----

The group will expand their activities outside Japan, releasing a second Korean single. Their concerts, _NiziU Live with U 2025 & 2026_, are set to take place in 21 cities during the second half of 2025.

NEXZ
----

After winning a “Top 5 New Artist” award at the Japan Gold Disc Awards, NEXZ also secured a spot in the Recording Academy’s “Top 8 K-Pop Rookies to Watch in 2025.” They will have new album releases and concerts in both Korea and Japan, alongside merchandise expansion featuring their NEXZOO character and official light sticks.

Other JYP Artists
-----------------

**VCHA** is preparing for a comeback in the first half of 2025 with localized content. **L2K** and **Project****C** are also set to debut, and the company plans to introduce new artists in 2026.

**Source:**[JYPE](https://www.jype.com/en/Board/Detail?gubun=irdata&jbst_sq=808&PgIndex=1)

Next Page

Kim Soo Hyun’s Upcoming K-Drama Reportedly Delayed, Sponsors Expected To Suffer Losses
======================================================================================

The series has now an uncertain release schedule.

![Image 6](https://image.koreaboo.com/2025/03/kshKnockoff-FI.jpg)

[News](https://www.koreaboo.com/news/)

![Image 7](https://www.koreaboo.com/wp-content/themes/KbooOS2/img/site_icon/koreaboo36.png)

Koreaboo

March 17th, 2025

_Disney+_’s upcoming K-Drama _Knockoff_, starring **Kim****Soo****Hyun**, is reportedly facing a delay following the actor’s recent controversy. Originally set for a production press conference next month with a release in the first half of the year, the series now has an uncertain schedule due to controversy surrounding its lead.

![Image 8: kim soo hyun queen of tears still](https://image.koreaboo.com/2025/03/kim-soo-hyun-queen-of-tears-still-1-925x617.jpg)

| _tvN_

_Knockoff_ follows a man whose life is upended by the 1997 Asian financial crisis, leading him to become a major figure in the counterfeit goods market. Kim Soo Hyun takes on the role of Kim Sung Joon, vice president of Saemmul Market, while **Jo****Bo****Ah** plays Song Hye Jung, a special judicial officer targeting counterfeit operations. With a significant budget and a second season already confirmed, the series had been generating considerable buzz.

![Image 9: knockoff](https://image.koreaboo.com/2025/03/knockoff.jpg)

| _Disney_

However, recent allegations that Kim Soo Hyun was romantically involved with the late actress **Kim Sae Ron** when she was underage have thrown the production into uncertainty. If the issue remains unresolved, the actor may be unable to attend promotional events, and in the worst case, the K-Drama’s release could even be reconsidered. _Disney_ _Korea_ has responded to such speculation by stating that a final release date has yet to be confirmed.

> The release schedule has not been finalized.
> 
> 
> —Disney Korea

![Image 10: knockoff presscon](https://image.koreaboo.com/2025/03/knockoff-presscon-640x426.jpg)

| _Disney_

Amid this uncertainty, brands that partnered with _Knockoff_ are also expected to take a financial hit. Among them is **Safety****Zone****Korea**, South Korea’s first-ever streetwear brand, which had invested in the project. CEO **Park****Ki****Pyo** expressed disappointment over the situation, stating that the company will wait for Disney’s decision before making an official statement.

> As a company that values youthful energy and innovative branding, we collaborated with Knockoff in its production. However, this unforeseen scandal has disrupted the project, which is truly regrettable. We will determine our official stance after Disney releases its decision.
> 
> 
> — Park Ki Pyo

With the future of _Knockoff_ in limbo, attention is now on whether Disney+ will move forward with the release or adjust its plans.

**Source:**[Kyunghyang](https://v.daum.net/v/20250317112807905)

**JYP Entertainment Corporation** ([Korean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Korean_language "Korean language"):JYP 엔터테인먼트) is a South Korean [multinational](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinational_corporation "Multinational corporation")[entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Entertainment "Entertainment") and [record label](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Record_label "Record label")[conglomerate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conglomerate_(company) "Conglomerate (company)") founded in 1997 by [J. Y. Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Jin-young "Park Jin-young"). Operating as a record label, talent agency, music production company, event management company, concert production company and music publishing house, it is one of the largest entertainment companies in South Korea. The company also operates subsidiary ventures and divisions internationally.

History
-------

### 1997–99: Formation and first generation K-pop artists

[![Image 10: An image of Park Jin-young, holding a microphone.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/75/Park_Jin-young_%28Founder_of_JYP_Entertainment%29_in_February_2011_from_acrofan.jpg/250px-Park_Jin-young_%28Founder_of_JYP_Entertainment%29_in_February_2011_from_acrofan.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Park_Jin-young_(Founder_of_JYP_Entertainment)_in_February_2011_from_acrofan.jpg)

[Park Jin-young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Jin-young "Park Jin-young"), founder of JYP Entertainment

JYP Entertainment was founded in 1997 by South Korean singer-songwriter [Park Jin-young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Jin-young "Park Jin-young"), named after his stage name, J. Y. Park, as Tae-Hong Planning Corporation. In 2001, the company was retitled as JYP Entertainment.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-7) In 1997, the company signed its first artist – [Pearl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pearl_(singer) "Pearl (singer)").

In 1999, entertainment company [SidusHQ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IHQ_(company) "IHQ (company)") introduced the future members of boy band [G.o.d](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.o.d "G.o.d") to Park, as their producer and mentor. In cooperation with SidusHQ, JYP Entertainment oversaw the formation of g.o.d, which would make their debut appearance on January 13, 1999.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-8) The group was managed by SidusHQ, with their first album, _[Chapter 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapter\_1\_(g.o.d\_album) "Chapter 1 (g.o.d album)")_, being produced by Park.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-9)

### 2000–09: Early success and second generation K-pop artists

In December 2000, JYP Entertainment signed [Rain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rain_(entertainer) "Rain (entertainer)") as a trainee, who made his debut two years later in May 2002.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-11) Rain would then rise to become a commercial success throughout and beyond Asia,[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-multiple-12) which was seen when his third studio album, _[It's Raining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/It%27s\_Raining\_(album) "It's Raining (album)")_, went on to record cumulative sales of over 1 million copies in seven Asian countries, including South Korea.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-13)

On December 27, 2002, the company's first boy group was a four-member vocal oriented group [Noel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noel_(band) "Noel (band)") which failed to attract popularity. The company then turned its focus towards the duo brothers [One Two](https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EC%9B%90%ED%88%AC "ko:원투") in 2003. In 2004, after the boy band [g.o.d](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/G.o.d "G.o.d")'s group contract with SidusHQ ended, they signed a contract with JYP Entertainment.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-14)

Other artists that debuted under JYP Entertainment, from 2000 to 2005 were [Park Ji-yoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Park_Ji-yoon "Park Ji-yoon"), [Byul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Byul "Byul"), Lim Jeong-hee, [Ryanga Rhanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Ryanga_Rhanga&action=edit&redlink=1 "Ryanga Rhanga (page does not exist)")[[ko](https://ko.wikipedia.org/wiki/%EB%9F%89%ED%98%84%EB%9F%89%ED%95%98 "ko:량현량하")], and [Ivy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivy_(South_Korean_singer) "Ivy (South Korean singer)"). In May 2006, the company formed its first girl group, [Wonder Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder_Girls "Wonder Girls"),[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-15) who became a commercial success and was the first South Korean group to enter the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") in 2009, with their song "[Nobody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nobody_(Wonder_Girls_song) "Nobody (Wonder Girls song)")".[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-billboard-16) Their success lead to a management deal with the [Jonas Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nine_West_Holdings "Nine West Holdings"), which led the group to open the [Jonas Brothers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonas_Brothers "Jonas Brothers")' [world tour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jonas_Brothers_World_Tour_2009 "Jonas Brothers World Tour 2009") in select cities.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-jobro-17)

In 2007, Rain left JYP Entertainment and established his own agency called [J. Tune Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Tune_Entertainment "J. Tune Entertainment").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-:2-18)

[![Image 11: An image of the Wonder Girls on the stage, wearing identical clothes.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/11/Wonder_Girls_from_acrofan.jpg/250px-Wonder_Girls_from_acrofan.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Wonder_Girls_from_acrofan.jpg)

[Wonder Girls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wonder_Girls "Wonder Girls") in 2008. The first South Korean group to enter the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-billboard-16)

In 2008, the competitive reality series _Hot Blood Men_ was created, pitting two teams of male trainees against each other for the chance to debut. The winning group, One Day, was later split into two boy bands, [2PM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2PM "2PM") and [2AM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2AM_(band) "2AM (band)"). Both debuted in the same year.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-19) 2AM was jointly contracted with [Big Hit Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Hit_Music "Big Hit Music").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-:0-20) Later in October, the JYP Beijing Center was opened, as the company's China branch. In that same year, the [Creative Artists Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Creative_Artists_Agency "Creative Artists Agency") included JYP Entertainment in its roster of high-profile clientele.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-22)

Expanding its endeavors into the drama production industry following in the footsteps of SM Entertainment Group's [SM C&C](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SM_Culture_%26_Contents "SM Culture & Contents") and CJ E&M's [Studio Dragon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Studio_Dragon "Studio Dragon") – JYP Entertainment jointly established the television drama production company Holym with Key East Entertainment in June 2009.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-23) Holym later announced its first major television drama production, _[Dream High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dream\_High "Dream High")_, in 2010.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-24)

### 2010–17: Joint ventures and third generation K-pop artists

In March 2010, JYP Entertainment made a joint venture with [SM Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SM_Entertainment "SM Entertainment"), [YG Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YG_Entertainment "YG Entertainment"), [Star Empire Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Empire_Entertainment "Star Empire Entertainment"), Media Line, CAN Entertainment and Music Factory Entertainment to establish KMP Holdings, the official distributor of releases from these companies.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-25) On December 28, 2010, JYP Entertainment became the largest shareholder of [J. Tune Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Tune_Entertainment "J. Tune Entertainment").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-:2-18)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-:3-26) The subsidiary AQ Entertainment was later formed and introduced the Chinese-Korean girl group [Miss A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_A "Miss A").

[![Image 12: An image of Miss A, with the logo of Armani Exchange at the back.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6e/Miss_A_2013.jpg/250px-Miss_A_2013.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Miss_A_2013.jpg)

[Miss A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_A "Miss A") in 2013. The first act to have their debut song reach atop the [Gaon Digital Chart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaon_Digital_Chart "Gaon Digital Chart").[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-27)

In November 2011, the American based subsidiary JYP Creative was established. Park invested approximately US$1.2 million in the branch. After a year of operation, the company saw a net loss of around US$1.5 million by the end of 2012, leading to the liquidation and closure of the branch, including the New York branch.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-28) The same year, [Park Jimin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie_(singer) "Jamie (singer)"), winner of the competitive TV series _[K-pop Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-pop\_Star\_season\_1 "K-pop Star season 1")_ and [Baek Yerin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baek_Yerin "Baek Yerin"), a female trainee and contestant on the show _Star King_, debuted as the duo [15&](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/15%26 "15&").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-29)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable\_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_]

In 2012, JYP Pictures signed a contract with China Eastern Performing Arts Group to co-produce a movie _Hold Your Hand_, featuring actors who were signed to JYP Entertainment.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-30)

[![Image 13: An image of GOT7, all wearing a black suit.](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/Got7_2019_New_Year%27s_greetings_07.jpg/250px-Got7_2019_New_Year%27s_greetings_07.jpg)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Got7_2019_New_Year%27s_greetings_07.jpg)

[Got7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Got7 "Got7") in 2019.

On June 20, 2013, the merger plan for the [publicly listed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_company "Public company") JYP Entertainment and the [non-listed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Private_company "Private company") JYP was announced.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-32) The merger was approved on October 17.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-33) Miss A and [Baek A-yeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baek_A-yeon "Baek A-yeon"), also joined JYP Entertainment due to the merger.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-AQEntertainment-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-35) On August 25, 2013, JYP Entertainment and [KeyEast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KeyEast "KeyEast") terminated their joint production enterprise, Holym.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-36)[_[unreliable source?](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable\_sources "Wikipedia:Reliable sources")_] On November 17, 2013, the company partnered with [Smilegate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smilegate "Smilegate") to promote the video game game _[Crossfire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crossfire\_(2007\_video\_game) "Crossfire (2007 video game)")_, with [2PM](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2PM "2PM") and [Miss A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miss_A "Miss A").[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-37)

In January 2014, the seven talent agencies behind [KMP Holdings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KMP_Holdings "KMP Holdings") formed a collective bond partnership and bought 13.48% of [KT Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KT_Music "KT Music")'s stocks, leaving [KT Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KT_Corporation "KT Corporation") with 49.99%.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-gaonchart1-38) In the same month, [Got7](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Got7 "Got7"), made their debut.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-kpopherald-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-40) 2AM's joint contract of [Big Hit Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Hit_Entertainment "Big Hit Entertainment") with JYP Entertainment later in April ended, after three of the 2AM members returned to JYP Entertainment, and member [Lee Chang-min](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Chang-min_(singer) "Lee Chang-min (singer)") stayed with Big Hit Entertainment, to continue his career and as part of the duo [Homme](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homme_(band) "Homme (band)").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-:0-20) In August, JYP Pictures and Dongyang World Culture Communication produced the drama _Dream Knight_, starring Got7 members.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-41) Season three _[K-pop Star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K-pop\_Star "K-pop Star")_ winner [Bernard Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernard_Park "Bernard Park") signed a contract with JYP Entertainment to start his solo career, and making his debut on October 6.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-42) On December 17, J.Y. Park sold the company's headquarters building in [Cheongdam-dong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheongdam-dong "Cheongdam-dong"), Seoul to Choi Ki-won, for approximately $7 million, on the term that JYP Entertainment will still use the building for three years on rent.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-44)

Joint ventures
--------------

JYP Entertainment's records are distributed worldwide by [The Orchard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Orchard_(company) "The Orchard (company)") since March 2019.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-98)

### KMP Holdings and KT Music

In March 2010, [KMP Holdings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KMP_Holdings "KMP Holdings") was established via a [joint venture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint_venture "Joint venture") between JYP Entertainment, [SM Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SM_Entertainment "SM Entertainment"), [YG Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YG_Entertainment "YG Entertainment"), Star Empire, Media Line, CAN Entertainment and Music Factory Entertainment. KMP Holdings was acquired by [KT Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genie_Music "Genie Music") in November 2012. In June 2013, KT Music absorbed KMP's distribution network. In January 2014, the seven talent agencies behind [KMP Holdings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KMP_Holdings "KMP Holdings") formed a collective bond partnership and bought 13.48% of [KT Music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KT_Music "KT Music")'s stocks, leaving [KT Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KT_Corporation "KT Corporation") with 49.99%.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-gaonchart1-38)

### United Asia Management

In 2011, JYP Entertainment joined forces with SM Entertainment, YG Entertainment, [KeyEast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KeyEast "KeyEast"), AMENT and Star J Entertainment to form United Asia Management in an effort to promote Korean pop music internationally.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-UAM-99)

### FLO

On January 31, 2018, [iRiver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IRiver "IRiver") announced its entry into the South Korean music industry. Together with parent company [SK Telecom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SK_Telecom "SK Telecom") and music labels SM Entertainment, JYP Entertainment and [Big Hit Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Hit_Entertainment "Big Hit Entertainment"), the company launched a new online music store, FLO, in the second half of 2018.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-100)

### Beijing Shinsung Entertainment

On April 5, 2017, Ocean Music and JYP Entertainment jointly established the Beijing Xin Sheng Entertainment Co., Ltd. for indoor recreational facilities operation, organization of cultural and artistic exchanges, film and television planning, and other aspects of cooperation. A few months later, [Park Jin-young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Y._Park "J. Y. Park"), [Jackson Wang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackson_Wang "Jackson Wang"), [Fei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fei_(singer) "Fei (singer)") and a 10-year-old JYP Chinese trainee went to China to record a roadshow-style audition show to recruit more trainees with the goal of creating a hip-hop oriented Chinese boy group. The name of the show was _Guaishushu Is Coming_, and the concept was to travel across different cities with large-scale auditions and then have a final round to select the members who will be trained in South Korea.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-qdaily.com-54)

### NCC Entertainment (NCC Station)

NCC Entertainment is a jointly produced management team by Tencent Music Corporation and JYP Beijing Cultural Exchange Ltd located in Beijing, China.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-qdaily.com-54) It is working to promote its Chinese artists more, despite the ban placed on Korean entertainment and to further promote the Chinese boy group, [Boy Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boy_Story "Boy Story") in China.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-101)

In September 2019, JYP Actors was closed, with its actors moving into a new start-up company, Npio Entertainment.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-:4-75)
*   **JYP Pictures**: The company's film and television drama production division founded in March 2011.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
    *   JYP Pictures Co., Ltd Korea: Established in 2013, it was closed by September 1, 2019.
    *   JYP Pictures Co., Ltd China: Established in 2014.

*   **JYP Creative**. The company's American subsidiary corporation, established in November 2011. It was liquidated in 2012, after a net loss of $1.5 million.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-USA-102)
*   **[J. Tune Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/J._Tune_Entertainment "J. Tune Entertainment")**: A South Korean record label and entertainment company founded by former JYP artist Rain in November 2007. In December 2010, JYP Entertainment had become the largest shareholder of J. Tune Entertainment.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-:3-26) In December 2013, J. Tune Entertainment was merged to JYP Entertainment.

Philanthropy
------------

During the [COVID-19 pandemic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic "COVID-19 pandemic"), JYP Entertainment donated US$410 thousand to the Community Chest of South Korea on February 28, 2020.[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-114) On March 8, 2022, the company made a donation [₩](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Korean_won "South Korean won")300 million to the Hope Bridge Disaster Relief Association, to help the victims of the massive wildfire that started in Uljin, Gyeongbuk which had spread to Samcheok, Gangwon.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-115) On February 12, 2023, the company donated ₩500 million through [World Vision International](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_Vision_International "World Vision International"), to help the aftermath of the [2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Turkey%E2%80%93Syria_earthquakes "2023 Turkey–Syria earthquakes").[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JYP_Entertainment#cite_note-116)

JYP Entertainment recently released an outlook for 2025. (Photo Credit: Instagram)

JYP Entertainment, a South Korean multinational entertainment and record label, recently pulled back the curtain on its plans for all the groups in 2025, setting the stage for yet another thrilling year in[K-pop.](https://www.news18.com/movies/new-k-pop-group-close-your-eyes-struggles-with-fans-overwhelming-attention-at-airport-aa-9175937.html) With a mix of new world tours of groups under the label and the release of new albums, K-pop fanatics can expect non-stop entertainment from the artists. Here’s what the groups under JYP Entertainment have in store for 2025.

**DAY6**

Recommended Stories
-------------------

After releasing two EPs in 2024, the now-quartet comprising Sungjin, Young K, Wonpil, and Dowoon made history by becoming the first band to perform at the Gocheok Sky Dome in 2024. The group will continue with their biggest world tour titled Forever Young in 2025, with its last show scheduled in May in Jakarta.

**TWICE**

In 2025, the nine-membered girl group will be busy with group, unit and solo activities. Their Japanese sub-unit MiSaMo recently achieved a milestone by becoming the fastest K-pop group to perform six dome concerts across three cities in Japan. A brand new world tour is also on the horizon for TWICE.

**Stray Kids**

Continuing with their meteoric rise in the global music industry, the eight-member band recorded some remarkable achievements last year. Their latest tour, Dominate, witnessed a whopping 2.2 million attendees across 55 shows in 34 locations around the world. Their dominance in U.S. sales charts remains unmatched, ranking second in overall CD sales, first among K-Pop artists, ranking at one on Billboard 200 for six consecutive albums and 3 times consecutively on the Billboard Hot 100. In 2025, Stray Kids is expected to release two albums.

**ITZY**

Fans of the quintet can expect both group and solo activities, including new albums and tours, in 2025. Moreover, with ITZY’s Yeji already making waves for her solo debut, fans can also expect another solo debut from the rest of the members.

**NMIXX**

The six-member K-pop girl group under JYP is set to drop a new mini album in 2025. Following this, they will also embark on a series of fan concerts across Latin America and Asia. Their ever-growing popularity has also led to an increase in their brand deals.

**KickFlip**

Names as one of the “Top 8 K-Pop Rookies to Watch in 2025" by the Recording Academy, the septet has been making waves both domestically and internationally. Debuting in January 2025 with the EP Flip It, Kick It, their streaming numbers have continued to surge. They already have a whopping 1 million followers on TikTok.

**NiziU**

The nine-membered Japanese girl group formed under the label is set to broaden their reach in 2025. They will be releasing their second Korean single soon. Moreover, the rookie group’s concerts NiziU Live with U 2025 & 2026, are scheduled to take place in 21 cities during the second half of 2025.

**NEXZ**

Fresh off winning the Top 5 New Artist award at the Japan Gold Disc Awards, NEXZ was also among the “Top 8 K-Pop Rookies to Watch in 2025" list released by the Recording Academy. With new album releases, Korean and Japanese concerts and a plan to expand their merchandise, the group surely has a lot in store for 2025.

**Others**

Another artist under the group, VCHA, is gearing up for their comeback in the first half of 2025 with localised content. L2K and Project C will make their debut. The company also has plans to expand its artist base by introducing new ones in 2026.
